builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Model-Based Online Decision Making via Generative Trajectory Planning
summary: GTP replaces from-scratch trajectory optimization at every decision step by sampling action sequences from a learned diffusion prior and refining them with learned dynamics, reward, and value models. The cost is training and maintaining four learned components (diffusion proposal, dynamics, reward, value) plus sampling-and-refinement overhead at inference, which exceeds the compute profile of a single policy forward pass. Failure modes include compounding model error in the learned dynamics over long horizons, proposal distribution mismatch when deployment states drift from training data, and degradation in environments where reward or dynamics are hard to model accurately.
rationale: This is model-based reinforcement learning for continuous control and robotic manipulation, not LLM inference or agent-system efficiency, so it falls outside the production scope of an AI/ML engineer deploying language models on constrained infrastructure.
technique: Generative trajectory planning with diffusion priors

Matches or exceeds state-of-the-art model-free, diffusion-policy, and model-based baselines on continuous control and long-horizon manipulation tasks, with no quantified improvement factor reported in the abstract.
